source.quote:
)I~recutive Orber.
0By virtue of the authority conferred upon me by Section 2 of the
act entitled "An Act limiting the hours of daily service of laborers and
mechanics employed upon work done for the United States, or for any
Territory, or for the District of Columbia, and for other purposes,"
approved June I19, 1912, the provisions and stipulations in said act are
hereby' waived, until January first, nineteen hundred and fifteen, as to any
contract or contracts entered into in connection with the construction of
the Isthmian Canal.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms: the eight-hour act's provisions and stipulations 'are hereby waived, until January first, nineteen hundred and fifteen' for Isthmian Canal construction contracts. Recorded as 1915-01-01, inclusive (runs through the end of that day) under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling; the exclusive alternative ends the waiver when that day began. Actor: EO 1547 itself.

research_rationale:
EO 1547 (June 19, 1912, William H. Taft), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan (archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false) and checked against the page image I rendered from the held PDF (sha256 2e446a81...; one page; printed number 'No. 1547', date 'June 19, 1912', signature 'Wm H Taft'). The OCR layer is complete; its errors ('I19' for 19, a stray apostrophe after 'hereby', '[No. 1547-.1') do not affect the operative words. Single operative command: under section 2 of the act of June 19, 1912 limiting the hours of daily service of laborers and mechanics on federal work (the 1912 eight-hour act), the act's provisions and stipulations 'are hereby waived, until January first, nineteen hundred and fifteen, as to any contract or contracts entered into in connection with the construction of the Isthmian Canal.' First end: by its own terms on 1915-01-01. Under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling the 'until' date is inclusive, so the waiver runs through the end of January 1, 1915; the alternative exclusive reading is that it stopped when that day began, leaving December 31, 1914 as its last day. Authority check: no held source shows section 2 of the 1912 act repealed or amended before 1915; the held text of EO 2663 (1917, jobs/wikisource-texts/output/texts/EO_2663.txt) invokes section 2 of the same act (37 Stat. 137), which corroborates that the authority still existed after this order's end. The act's own effective-date clause is not held; it does not affect the end. The order states its own date, so its end does not depend on when the canal construction contracts were completed.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end is held. Candidates considered and not shown to extinguish the waiver: the Panama Canal Act of August 24, 1912 and EO 1885 (January 27, 1914, permanent organization of the Panama Canal) with EO 1888 (February 2, 1914, conditions of employment). The waiver attaches to contracts for canal construction, not to the Isthmian Canal Commission, and neither order's held summary or text names EO 1547 or the 1912 act's waiver; under the owner's rule a later general instrument ends a command only if something shows it extinguished that command, and nothing held does. The Panama Canal Act's text is not held. No extension: census titles, the WPA 1944 numbered list and the full text of all 2,750 ProQuest scan texts were searched on 2026-10-28 for Isthmian or Panama Canal orders touching eight-hour or hours-of-labor rules between 1912 and 1916; the only hits were EO 1547 itself, EO 2514 (January 15, 1917, Canal Zone leave rules, effective December 31, 1916) and EO 4459 (1926, Canal overtime pay), none of which names this waiver or acts before 1915. A citation search of every held order text for 'No. 1547' or 'Order 1547' found only Proclamation No. 1547 of 1919 (Scotts Bluff), a different instrument. The date is a fixed term of the waiver, not a deadline on another act.","independent_command_check":"No independent command survives. The recital of section 2 of the 1912 act is authority, not a command. The waiver has no proviso imposing a separate continuing duty.","savings_check":"Contracts entered into while the waiver ran could lawfully omit the eight-hour stipulations, and work done under them was lawful. Where such a contract continued after January 1, 1915, its terms stood as made; that is an accrued effect of a contract formed under the waiver, carried by the contract and the 1912 act, and it does not keep the order operative, because the order commands nothing after its stated date. Pay for hours worked flows from the contracts and statute, not from the order. No held source shows any contract affected after 1915; this residual is a disclosed qualification, not a finding.","scope_check":"Whole order is one clause: a waiver for one class of contracts with one stated term. No partial amendment, extension or revocation of any part is held or found."}

savings_residuals.reason: Contracts entered into while the waiver ran could lawfully omit the eight-hour stipulations, and work done under them was lawful. Where such a contract continued after January 1, 1915, its terms stood as made; that is an accrued effect of a contract formed under the waiver, carried by the contract and the 1912 act, and it does not keep the order operative, because the order commands nothing after its stated date. Pay for hours worked flows from the contracts and statute, not from the order. No held source shows any contract affected after 1915; this residual is a disclosed qualification, not a finding.

source.quote:
)xecuttve Orber
It is hereby ordered that the several executive departments and independent
Government establishments in the District of Columbia, including the Government
Printing Office and the Navy Yard and Stations, be closed on Saturday, December
24, 1927, and all clerks and other employees in the Federal service in the District
of Columbia, except those who may for special public reasons be excepted from the
provisions of this Order, or those whose absence from duty would be inconsistent
with the provisions of existing law, are hereby excused from duty on that day.
This Order is not to be deemed as establishing a precedent.
CALVIN COOLIDGE
THE WHITE HOUSE,
December 16, 1927.
[No. 47821
Trlu
97f

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the close of Saturday, December 24, 1927, the only day on which it closes the District offices and excuses employees ('be closed on Saturday, December 24, 1927 ... are hereby excused from duty on that day'). Actor: EO 4782 itself. The dossier holds no own-terms record for this order, so the end cites the order's complete held text, which contains the stated day.

research_rationale:
EO 4782 (December 16, 1927, Calvin Coolidge), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan (archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false) and checked against the page image I rendered from the held PDF (sha256 cf42ef50...; one page; printed 'No. 4782', date 'December 16, 1927', signature 'Calvin Coolidge'; handwritten marginal note 'Holidays'). The OCR layer is complete; its trailing noise ('[No. 47821', 'Trlu', '97f') is the printed number and the handwritten note, not order text. It closes the executive departments and independent establishments in the District of Columbia, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, on Saturday, December 24, 1927, and excuses federal employees in the District from duty that day, except those excepted for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law. Its last sentence says 'This Order is not to be deemed as establishing a precedent.' The type label closing_mourning fits. First end: by its own terms at the close of 1927-12-24, the only day it governs. A reader who dates cessation to the first day without effect would write 1927-12-25; this claim records 1927-12-24, the day through whose end the order ran, consistent with the owner's inclusive reading of stated dates. The census register gives only the year; the date December 16, 1927 comes from the scan and agrees with the WPA 1944 list ('1928 CSR 78').

The only related order found is EO 5008 (1928), which closes the same offices on December 24, 1928; it is a new one-day order, not an extension or amendment of EO 4782, and does not name it.
